rules.statement: a correction's predecessor id names an event in the chain
the recorded predecessor digest is the predecessor's canonical digest
each event has at most one successor
no chain revisits an event and no predecessor points forward
a correction's predecessor is about the same subject
a subject has at most one root assertion
a correction's old value is the predecessor's accepted value
an assertion does not supersede an event

decision.statement: DENY if any obligation is UNKNOWN; else DENY if no obligation is required; else ADMIT iff every required obligation is MET; else DENY.

limits: The enumeration is finite. Only decision-policy (4**8 = 65,536) is the whole state space of its function; decision-small, threshold and correction are declared finite domains and cannot prove the rule for inputs outside them.

The enumeration covers decision functions over abstract states and declared models, not the whole tool: record reading, predicates, applicability, pins, signatures, roles and history witnesses are outside it.
The reference shares an author with the implementation, so agreement is a shared reading, not independent verification (Earned Trust Article 5).
No machine-checked theorem exists: no TLA+, Coq, Lean or Kani proof, and no correspondence between this model and a compiled binary (Article 7).

rules.name: obligation-state-vocabulary
rules.statement: An obligation's recorded state is exactly one of MET, UNMET, UNKNOWN or NOT_APPLICABLE. No other state is admissible, and a state vector containing one is unspecified rather than decided.

rules.name: conjunction
rules.statement: The decision is ADMIT if and only if the required set is non-empty and every required obligation's state is MET; otherwise it is DENY. There is no score, weight, count of passing obligations, threshold or aggregation key that contributes to the decision.

rules.name: unknown-is-a-refusal
rules.statement: An obligation whose state is UNKNOWN makes the decision DENY whether or not the obligation is required. UNKNOWN is never read as MET and never as NOT_APPLICABLE: an obligation nobody could evaluate is a machinery defect in either case.

rules.name: required-inapplicable-denies
rules.statement: NOT_APPLICABLE on a required obligation is not a pass: only MET satisfies a required obligation, so a required obligation that is inapplicable denies. NOT_APPLICABLE on a non-required obligation does not decide.

rules.name: no-required-obligation-denies
rules.statement: A state vector with no required obligation admits nothing. Denial by default: an empty required set is not an all-met proof.

rules.name: canonical-order-independence
rules.statement: The decision is a pure function of the obligation state vector and the policy's required set. Permuting the state vector and its required flags together changes no decision; canonical (ascending-id) order is for recording, not for deciding.

rules.name: determinism
rules.statement: Two evaluations of the same state vector and required set return the same decision. No clock, random source or ambient state enters.

rules.name: threshold-distinct-domains
rules.statement: A k-of-n threshold is MET if and only if the number of distinct established trust domains among verified, role-valid, fresh, non-candidate approvals is at least k. An approval's domain label is a lookup key only: two labels whose domain records share an establishment record (path, sha256) are one domain. A duplicate approval on one domain counts once, and one identity contributes at most one domain.

rules.name: correction-chain-binding
rules.statement: An event is admissible if and only if every binding rule holds: its predecessor id names a stored event, the recorded predecessor digest is that event's canonical digest, each predecessor has at most one successor, no chain revisits an event, a subject has at most one root assertion, a correction names a predecessor about the same subject, and a correction's old value is the predecessor's accepted value. The original is never modified.

subject: the decision rules of the release verifier: the obligation conjunction, the distinct-trust-domain threshold and correction-chain admission
